full: I am going to call her later.
rule: going to becomes gonna before a verb.

full: I want to see the results.
rule: want to becomes wanna.

full: I have got to finish this today.
rule: got to becomes gotta.

full: Do you want to come with us?
rule: do you shrinks to d'you or dya.
what are you can sound like whatcha.
d + you blends into dj: didja.
let me becomes lemme.

full: I do not know where it is.
rule: don't know becomes dunno.
give me becomes gimme.
should have becomes shoulda; the have is reduced.

full: We could have taken the bus.
rule: could have becomes coulda.
kind of becomes kinda.

full: I have a lot of work.
rule: lot of becomes lotta; of is reduced to a.
A final consonant links to the next vowel: turn_it_off.
Consonant-to-vowel linking joins the words.
t between two consonants is often dropped.
h in he, him, her is often dropped inside a sentence.
him loses its h: tellim.
In American English, t between vowels becomes a quick d-like sound.
ought to becomes oughta.
